name: WA-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+39 partisan lean makes a Republican win nearly impossible
Jayapal is a well-funded incumbent with $1.8M on hand versus Sheth's $5K
Prediction markets price Jayapal at 97% to win
Challenger has raised only about $12K with no outside support
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Jayapal: a D+39 seat, a two-term-plus incumbent, and a massive financial advantage over a barely funded challenger. Markets agree, pricing her near certain, so the forecast sits slightly above the baseline margin given her resource edge.
model.watch: A major late scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Seattle-area WA-07 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+39. Incumbent Pramila Jayapal is running for another term and holds every structural advantage: name recognition, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of more than $2.5 million raised against roughly $12,000 for Republican Nirav Sheth, who has just $5,000 in the bank and no outside backing.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Jayapal about a 97% chance of winning. With no competitive signals in evidence, the seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the only uncertainty being the exact size of her victory margin.
